claim: Cellular redox status affects diverse cellular functions, including proliferation, protein homeostasis, and aging.
source: Cellular redox status affects diverse cellular functions, including proliferation, protein homeostasis, and aging.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific understanding.

claim: Individual differences in redox status can give rise to distinct sub-populations even among cells with identical genetic backgrounds.
source: Thus, individual differences in redox status can give rise to distinct sub-populations even among cells with identical genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This is a claim made in the abstract based on the study's findings.

claim: The study created a novel methodology to track redox status at single cell resolution using the redox-sensitive probe Grx1-roGFP2.
source: Here, we have created a novel methodology to track redox status at single cell resolution using the redox-sensitive probe Grx1-roGFP2.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the methodology developed in the study.

claim: The method allows identification and sorting of sub-populations with different oxidation levels in either the cytosol, mitochondria or peroxisomes.
source: Our method allows identification and sorting of sub-populations with different oxidation levels in either the cytosol, mitochondria or peroxisomes.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the developed methodology.

claim: Starting in late logarithmic growth, cells of the same age have a bi-modal distribution of oxidation status.
source: We report that, starting in late logarithmic growth, cells of the same age have a bi-modal distribution of oxidation status.
evidence: This is a key finding reported in the abstract.

claim: Three key proteins (Hsp30, Dhh1, and Pnc1) affect basal oxidation levels and may serve as first line of defense proteins in redox homeostasis.
source: A comparative proteomic analysis between these populations identified three key proteins, Hsp30, Dhh1, and Pnc1, which affect basal oxidation levels and may serve as first line of defense proteins in redox homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the proteomic analysis with speculative interpretation.

claim: Oxidative stress has been found to correlate with the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), protein aggregation, and apoptosis.
source: Oxidative stress has been found to correlate with the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), protein aggregation, and apoptosis (Madeo et al., 1999; Squier, 2001), as well as a number of other physiological changes that ultimately occur in a heterogenic manner.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Grx1-roGFP2 senses the glutathione redox potential.
source: One prominent redox sensor is the redox-sensitive GFP variant (roGFP) fused to human Glutaredoxin 1 (Grx1) known as Grx1-roGFP2 which senses the glutathione redox potential, with additional variants targeting it to organelles such as the mitochondria or peroxisome.
evidence: This describes the function of the Grx1-roGFP2 probe based on established knowledge.

claim: roGFP-based sensors have been used to conduct real-time measurements of redox potentials in bacteria, C. elegans, plant, and mammalian cells.
source: These and other similar probes have been used to conduct real-time measurements of redox potentials in bacteria (van der Heijden and Finlay, 2015), C. elegans (Braeckman et al., 2016), plant (Meyer et al., 2007), and mammalian cells (Dooley et al., 2004), by monitoring differences in oxidative status under a range of diverse conditions.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Detection of roGFP redox-dependent fluorescence has generally been based either on imaging individual cells by microscopy, or by measuring the total fluorescence signals of cells in suspension by using plate readers.
source: Detection of roGFP redox-dependent fluorescence has generally been based either on imaging individual cells by microscopy, or by measuring the total fluorescence signals of cells in suspension by using plate readers.
evidence: This describes the existing methods for roGFP detection based on established practices.

claim: Neither microscopy nor plate reader approaches enable high spatiotemporal resolution in widescale tracking of cell to cell diversity, nor subsequent isolation of cells based on their redox status.
source: However, neither approach enables high spatiotemporal resolution in widescale tracking of cell to cell diversity, nor subsequent isolation of cells based on their redox status.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of existing methods.

claim: Populations of genetically identical cells are heterogeneous in their protein and gene expression.
source: Over the last decade, numerous studies have pointed to the fact that populations of genetically identical cells are heterogeneous in their protein and gene expression (Elowitz et al., 2002; Maamar et al., 2007), exhibiting an array of differences in cellular behavior and in varying abilities to respond to changing environments (Ackermann, 2015; Altschuler et al., 2010; Avery, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Cell-to-cell variability is considered to be one of the crucial features in the evolution of new survival strategies in fluctuating environments.
source: This cell-to-cell variability is considered to be one of the crucial features in the evolution of new survival strategies in fluctuating environments (Altschuler et al., 2010), antibiotic treatment (Gefen and Balaban, 2009), pathogen progression (Avraham et al., 2015; Lieberman et al., 2014) and other processes.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The cell-to-cell heterogeneity of redox status within a population of synchronized cells with an identical genetic background has not yet been explored.
source: However, the cell-to-cell heterogeneity of redox status within a population of synchronized cells (i.e. cells that have a shared chronological age) with an identical genetic background has not yet been explored.
evidence: This identifies a gap in the existing literature.

claim: The study developed a highly sensitive methodology based on the Grx1-fused roGFP2 redox sensor that uses flow cytometry to measure the redox state of individual cells within a heterogeneous Saccharomyces cerevisiae population during chronological aging.
source: Here, we developed a highly sensitive methodology based on the Grx1-fused roGFP2 redox sensor that uses flow cytometry to measure the redox state of individual cells within a heterogeneous Saccharomyces cerevisiae (henceforth referred to as yeast) population during chronological aging.
evidence: This describes the methodology developed in the study.

claim: The proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of reduced and oxidized cells differ within a yeast population.
source: We show that the proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of reduced and oxidized cells differ within a yeast population, in addition to corresponding changes in growth and cellular division.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's proteomic and transcriptomic analyses.

claim: Comparative proteomic analysis identified three key proteins: the chaperone Hsp30, the helicase Dhh1, and the nicotinamidase Pnc1, which affect basal oxidation levels.
source: Comparative proteomic analysis identified three key proteins: the chaperone Hsp30, the helicase Dhh1, and the nicotinamidase Pnc1, which affect basal oxidation levels and might serve as first line of defense proteins in glutathione-dependent redox homeostasis.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: The ratio between the oxidized and reduced yeast subpopulations changes during chronological aging.
source: We also demonstrate that although the ratio between the oxidized and reduced yeast subpopulations changes during chronological aging, the major features, including the transcriptome and proteome, remain linked to the redox status through 72 hr.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's temporal analysis.

claim: The major features, including the transcriptome and proteome, remain linked to the redox status through 72 hr.
source: We also demonstrate that although the ratio between the oxidized and reduced yeast subpopulations changes during chronological aging, the major features, including the transcriptome and proteome, remain linked to the redox status through 72 hr.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's temporal analysis.

claim: There is a threshold of oxidation, above which the cell cannot maintain redox homeostasis according to the glutathione-based probe.
source: By using cell imaging, we further show that there is a threshold of oxidation, above which the cell cannot maintain redox homeostasis (according to the glutathione-based probe).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell imaging experiments.

claim: Once a mother cell is close to or above the oxidation threshold, it passes the oxidized state onto the daughter cell.
source: Finally, microscopic observations of budding cells show that once a mother cell is close to or above this threshold, it passes the oxidized state onto the daughter cell, which starts its life from a high, inherited oxidation level.
evidence: This is a finding from the microscopic observations.

claim: Cellular redox status has been suggested to be correlated with cell function and longevity.
source: Cellular redox status has been suggested to be correlated with cell function and longevity (Reverter-Branchat et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Measurements of cellular oxidation levels tend to be based on a global assessment of protein oxidation and the cellular redox status of the entire cellular population.
source: Measurements of cellular oxidation levels tend to be based on a global assessment of protein oxidation and the cellular redox status of the entire cellular population (Kojer et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes existing measurement approaches with a citation.

claim: Grx1-roGFP2 has a characteristic fluorescence according to a redox-dependent conformational change that leads to an alternating peak intensity at 405 and 488 nm.
source: To do so, we utilized the redox sensitive GFP variant Grx1-roGFP2 (Figure 1A) (Morgan et al., 2011), which has a characteristic fluorescence according to a redox-dependent conformational change (Hanson et al., 2004) that leads to an alternating peak intensity at 405 and 488 nm.
evidence: This describes the properties of the Grx1-roGFP2 probe with citations.

claim: The fluorescence spectrum of cells between 360 and 495 nm shows alternating peak pattern at 405 and 488 nm under oxidizing or reducing conditions.
source: In order to verify Grx1-roGFP2 expression patterns in our yeast cells, we measured the fluorescence spectrum of cells between 360 and 495 nm, following emission at 535 nm using plate reader analysis, under either oxidizing or reducing conditions (Figure 1B). In agreement with previous studies, we identified the alternating peak pattern at 405 and 488 nm (Hanson et al., 2004), which indicates the differences in ratio between 405 and 488 nm under oxidizing or reducing conditions.
evidence: This is a finding from the plate reader analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The 405/488 nm ratios of reduced and oxidized cells were significantly different and could be characterized using linear fits with a slope of 3.57 for oxidized and 0.6 for reduced cells.
source: The 405/488 nm ratios of reduced and oxidized cells were significantly different and could be characterized using linear fits with a slope of 3.57 for oxidized and 0.6 for reduced cells (the correlation coefficients (R2) were 0.99 and 0.97 for oxidized and reduced cells, respectively) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: The discrete difference between the oxidized and reduced states enabled creation of gates for oxidized and reduced cells.
source: The discrete difference between the oxidized and reduced states enabled us to create gates for oxidized and reduced cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), such that we could sort and characterize yeast subpopulations according to their redox status.
evidence: This describes the methodology enabled by the observed differences.

claim: The approach was also applied to organelle-specific redox sensors, such as the mitochondrial Grx1-roGFP2-Su9 and the peroxisomal Grx1-roGFP2-SKL, revealing a similar redox sensitivity.
source: This approach was also applied to organelle-specific redox sensors, such as the mitochondrial Grx1-roGFP2-Su9 (Kojer et al., 2012) and the peroxisomal Grx1-roGFP2-SKL (Elbaz-Alon et al., 2014), revealing a similar redox sensitivity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from applying the method to organelle-specific sensors.

claim: Cellular oxidation increased with chronological age when using the cytosolic Grx1-roGFP2 redox sensor.
source: To examine the ability of our flowcytometry-based method to monitor the age-related oxidation in yeast cells, we first used the cytosolic Grx1-roGFP2 redox sensor to evaluate the average glutathione-dependent cellular redox changes of the wild type yeast strain over four days of growth in standard medium enriched with casein digest under aerobic conditions (as described in Materials and methods). As expected, cellular oxidation increased with chronological age (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the chronological aging experiment shown in Figure 2A.

claim: When using the mitochondrial matrix sensor (Grx1-roGFP2-Su9), there was a smaller age-dependent difference in mitochondrial versus cytosolic oxidation.
source: Interestingly, when using the mitochondrial matrix sensor (Grx1-roGFP2-Su9) on the same wild type strain, we identified a smaller age-dependent difference in mitochondrial versus cytosolic oxidation, suggesting a robustness of mitochondrial antioxidant behavior during chronological aging (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the mitochondrial sensor experiment shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There is a robustness of mitochondrial antioxidant behavior during chronological aging.
source: Interestingly, when using the mitochondrial matrix sensor (Grx1-roGFP2-Su9) on the same wild type strain, we identified a smaller age-dependent difference in mitochondrial versus cytosolic oxidation, suggesting a robustness of mitochondrial antioxidant behavior during chronological aging (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mitochondrial oxidation data.

claim: There is a clear bi-modal distribution of reduced and oxidized subpopulations when examining the distribution of the fluorescence intensity ratios of Grx1-roGFP2 over four days of growth.
source: When we examined the distribution of the fluorescence intensity ratios of Grx1-roGFP2 (at 405 and 488 nm) over four days of growth under chronological aging conditions (24, 48, 72, 96 hr), we found a clear bi-modal distribution of reduced and oxidized subpopulations (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the distribution analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: As the culture aged, the fraction of reduced cells decreased while the fraction of oxidized cells increased.
source: As the culture aged, the fraction of reduced cells decreased while the fraction of oxidized cells increased.
evidence: This is an observation from the temporal analysis.

claim: The largest shift from reduction to oxidation occurs after 48 hr of growth.
source: Notably, the largest shift from reduction to oxidation occurs after 48 hr of growth.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the temporal analysis.

claim: A majority of cells remained reduced over time, suggesting that despite the culture being in the stationary phase, some cells nonetheless undergo replication and produce reduced cells.
source: Thus, we were able to monitor the time-dependent shift from reduced to oxidized subpopulations as the yeast cells aged. However, we noted that a majority of cells remained reduced over time, suggesting that despite the culture being in the stationary phase, some cells nonetheless undergo replication and produce reduced cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed data.

claim: The reduced cells exhibited a significantly faster minimal doubling time (MDT) at 48 and 72 hr relative to the oxidized population of the same age.
source: The subpopulations of the same chronological age (i.e. cultures grown for 48 or 72 hr before sorting), displayed characteristic differences in their recovery growth rate, whereas the reduced cells exhibited a significantly faster minimal doubling time (MDT) at 48 and 72 hr relative to the oxidized population of the same age (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the growth rate analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The differences in growth rate are indicative of an apparent impairment in the oxidized population's ability to rapidly divide and grow as a culture, rather than any inherent inability to enter the logarithmic growth stage.
source: These differences are indicative of an apparent impairment in the oxidized population's ability to rapidly divide and grow as a culture, rather than any inherent inability to enter the logarithmic growth stage (as evidenced by the similar lag phase lengths, Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the growth data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: After 96 hr, both subpopulations had ostensibly similar doubling times following longer lag phases than younger cells.
source: After 96 hr, both subpopulations had ostensibly similar doubling times following longer lag phases than younger cells (Figure 3B), consistent with the fact that these were relatively old cells with decreased vitality, particularly among the oxidized cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the growth analysis at 96 hr shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The oxidized population displayed on average 3–4.5 times more division scars than the reduced population.
source: The differences in the growth rates were further supported by a difference in the average number of division or bud scars per cell (Figure 3C). The oxidized population displayed on average 3–4.5 times more division scars than the reduced population, which typically displayed cells with no more than one scar (Figure 3C), indicating that the oxidized subpopulation had undergone multiple divisions in contrast to the reduced subpopulation.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the bud scar analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The oxidized subpopulation displayed a far lower budding rate relative to the reduced subpopulation, in which approximately 30% of cells at 48 hr were observed to be in the process of budding.
source: Furthermore, the oxidized subpopulation displayed a far lower budding rate relative to the reduced subpopulation, in which approximately 30% of cells at 48 hr were observed to be in the process of budding (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the budding analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: There is a correlation between the degree of cellular oxidation and division events in the stationary stage.
source: These results suggest a correlation between the degree of cellular oxidation and division events in the stationary stage.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the budding and division data.

claim: The OCR of the oxidized cells was consistently 1.8–2 fold lower than the reduced population.
source: The OCR of the oxidized cells was consistently 1.8–2 fold lower than the reduced population (Figure 4A), while their ECAR rate was 2–2.8 fold higher (Figure 4B), suggesting a strong shift from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis reminiscent of the Warburg effect in the oxidized subpopulation.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the Seahorse assay shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The ECAR rate of oxidized cells was 2–2.8 fold higher than the reduced population.
source: The OCR of the oxidized cells was consistently 1.8–2 fold lower than the reduced population (Figure 4A), while their ECAR rate was 2–2.8 fold higher (Figure 4B), suggesting a strong shift from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis reminiscent of the Warburg effect in the oxidized subpopulation.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the Seahorse assay shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There is a strong shift from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis reminiscent of the Warburg effect in the oxidized subpopulation.
source: The OCR of the oxidized cells was consistently 1.8–2 fold lower than the reduced population (Figure 4A), while their ECAR rate was 2–2.8 fold higher (Figure 4B), suggesting a strong shift from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis reminiscent of the Warburg effect in the oxidized subpopulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the OCR and ECAR data.

claim: Decreased oxygen consumption is strongly correlated with decreased cell growth of the oxidized subpopulation as compared to the reduced subpopulation.
source: Decreased oxygen consumption is strongly correlated with decreased cell growth of the oxidized subpopulation as compared to the reduced subpopulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation correlating the OCR and growth data.

claim: During early growth (after 24 hr incubation), the subpopulation of cells with a lower bud scar count has a ratio that closely resembles early growth under standard conditions, with a strong peak distributed around reduced ratios.
source: During early growth (after 24 hr incubation) (Figure 5B), two subpopulations emerge with regards to bud scar count, with one demonstrating a stronger expression of the lectin dye associated with a higher bud scar count (labeled as p1 in Figure 5B) and one with lower bud scar counts (labeled as p3 in Figure 5B). Among the GFP-positive cells the subpopulation of cells with a lower bud scar count has a ratio that closely resembles early growth under standard conditions as described earlier, with a strong peak distributed around reduced ratios, and a very minor subpopulation in the oxidized range (6.5% in the representative figure) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from the mother enrichment program analysis shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: The high bud scar subpopulation clearly falls into the oxidized range (87.8% in the representative figure) during early growth.
source: The high bud scar subpopulation, meanwhile, clearly falls into the oxidized range (87.8% in the representative figure), with distribution of the corresponding 405/488 nm ratios indicating a wide peak around ratios higher than 4 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from the mother enrichment program analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: A small minority of the high bud scar subpopulation is nonetheless reduced, despite having undergone multiple divisions.
source: However, a small minority of the subpopulation is nonetheless reduced, despite having undergone multiple divisions.
evidence: This is an observation from the mother enrichment program analysis.

claim: During late growth (after 72 hr incubation), the subpopulation that has undergone multiple divisions is overwhelmingly oxidized (87.6%), with a very small group of reduced cells (3%).
source: During late growth (after 72 hr incubation), a marked shift occurs towards cells with an increased number of bud scars (p1, Figure 5E), with a smaller subpopulation of cells remaining with fewer scars (p3, Figure 5E) (i.e., cells that have divided fewer times during growth). Similar to early growth, the subpopulation that has undergone multiple divisions is overwhelmingly oxidized (87.6%), with a very small group of reduced cells (3%) (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is a finding from the mother enrichment program analysis shown in Figure 5E,G.

claim: Among the subpopulation with a lower bud scar count at late growth, a larger fraction of young mothers underwent oxidation (36.4 vs 6.5%) compared to early growth, suggesting a transition from the largely reduced population at early growth to the highly oxidized population at late growth.
source: Interestingly, among the subpopulation with a lower bud scar count, we detect two distinct populations of cells with reduced and oxidized ratios. Unlike the early growth sample, a larger fraction of young mothers underwent oxidation (36.4 vs 6.5%), suggesting a transition from the largely reduced population at early growth to the highly oxidized population at late growth (Figure 5F vs Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing the mother enrichment program data at different time points.

claim: Cellular oxidation is not embedded solely in number of divisions, but also in the duration of the stationary phase (chronological aging).
source: Thus, cellular oxidation is not embedded solely in number of divisions, but also in the duration of the stationary phase (chronological aging).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mother enrichment program data.

claim: There is a strong, though not absolute, correlation between replicative aging and redox state.
source: Together, these results strengthen the correlation described earlier between the cellular redox state and cell divisions, here identifying a link between cells that have undergone multiple divisions and a strong tendency towards oxidation, though not an exclusive one. We observe that despite undergoing many replications, a small subpopulation of the mother cells remains 'eternally reduced', while there is a complementary subpopulation of cells that have divided relatively few times that begin life in an oxidized state. This suggests a strong, though not absolute, correlation between replicative aging and redox state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mother enrichment program data.

claim: There is a shift in the redox ratio between the subpopulation of highly divided cells at early growth as compared to late growth, while the degree of cell divisions itself does not change.
source: Furthermore, we observe a shift in the redox ratio between the subpopulation of highly divided cells at early growth as compared to late growth, while the degree of cell divisions itself (as identified by Texas Red-X intensity) does not change.
evidence: This is an observation from the mother enrichment program analysis.

claim: This points to additional redox changes unrelated to division and replicative events, correlated instead with chronological aging.
source: This points to additional redox changes unrelated to division and replicative events, correlated instead with chronological aging.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed shift in redox ratio.

claim: Using MaxQuant analysis and a stringent filter, 3389 proteins were identified, of which 1019 were identified in all four subpopulations at least twice.
source: Using MaxQuant analysis and a stringent filter, we identified 3389 proteins, of which 1019 were identified in all four subpopulations at least twice (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the proteomic analysis.

claim: According to the Uniprot-based cellular localization annotation, the majority of identified proteins were cytosolic (51%), where the remaining proteins were associated with the mitochondria (16%), nucleus (19%), ER (6%), Golgi vesicles (4%), vacuole (3%), stress granules, P-bodies (0.7%) and peroxisomes (1%).
source: According to the Uniprot-based cellular localization annotation, the majority of our identified proteins were cytosolic (51%), where the remaining proteins were associated with the mitochondria (16%), nucleus (19%), ER (6%), Golgi vesicles (4%), vacuole (3%), stress granules, P-bodies (0.7%) and peroxisomes (1%) (Supplementary file 2, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the proteomic analysis.

claim: The protein distribution is consistent with general distributions of yeast proteins, suggesting that no dramatic expansion or shrinking of an organelle occurred during the experiment.
source: This is consistent with general distributions of yeast proteins (47% cytosol, 15% mitochondria and 13% ER and secretory vesicles [Kumar et al., 2002]) suggesting that no dramatic expansion or shrinking of an organelle occurred during the experiment.
evidence: This is an interpretation comparing the observed distribution to known yeast protein distributions.

claim: Clustering of average LFQ intensities for all sample groups revealed that the protein expression profiles were similar between groups with a similar redox status, regardless of the sample age (48 or 72 hr).
source: Clustering of average LFQ intensities for all sample groups revealed that the protein expression profiles were similar between groups with a similar redox status, regardless of the sample age (48 or 72 hr) (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The two largest clusters, comprising more than 600 proteins, showed that the differential expression between oxidized and reduced subpopulations remained consistent for over two days.
source: The two largest clusters, comprising more than 600 proteins, showed that the differential expression between oxidized and reduced subpopulations remained consistent for over two days (Figure 6A, clusters 3 and 10, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Annotation enrichment analysis of the proteins comprising the two largest clusters suggested that the reduced cells (48 and 72 hr) had an increased presence of proteins involved in energy production, including mitochondrial proteins, protein biogenesis and protein degradation.
source: Annotation enrichment analysis of the proteins comprising these two clusters suggested that the reduced cells (48 and 72 hr) had an increased presence of proteins involved in energy production, including mitochondrial proteins, protein biogenesis and protein degradation (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from the annotation enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The reduced cells having increased presence of proteins involved in energy production corresponds with the finding that the reduced subpopulation had an elevated growth rate and was in the process of division.
source: This corresponds with our previous finding that the reduced subpopulation had an elevated growth rate and was in the process of division.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the proteomic findings to the growth data.

claim: The oxidized cells had a distinct subset of proteins regulating protein folding and redox homeostasis, alongside oxidoreductases and NAD binding proteins.
source: The oxidized cells had a distinct subset of proteins regulating protein folding and redox homeostasis, alongside oxidoreductases and NAD binding proteins (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from the annotation enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: A subset of 199 proteins showed statistically significant different expression profiles between the reduced and oxidized populations after 48 hr growth.
source: We identified a subset of 199 proteins showing statistically significant different expression profiles between the reduced and oxidized populations after 48 hr growth and 149 proteins after 72 hr growth (Figure 6C, Supplementary files 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the statistical analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: 149 proteins showed statistically significant different expression profiles between the reduced and oxidized populations after 72 hr growth.
source: We identified a subset of 199 proteins showing statistically significant different expression profiles between the reduced and oxidized populations after 48 hr growth and 149 proteins after 72 hr growth (Figure 6C, Supplementary files 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the statistical analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The proteome of the oxidized cells contained significant upregulation of proteins induced by a variety of stresses (Gre1, Sro9, Hsp150), as well as proteins directly involved in redox homeostasis (thioredoxin peroxidase Tsa2, Tma19).
source: Specifically, the proteome of the oxidized cells contained significant upregulation of proteins induced by a variety of stresses (Gre1, Sro9, Hsp150), as well as proteins directly involved in redox homeostasis (thioredoxin peroxidase Tsa2, Tma19).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: The oxidized cells displayed an upregulated expression of ribosomal proteins, in which 21 proteins belonging to 40 and 60S ribosomal subunits were identified.
source: Interestingly, the oxidized cells displayed an upregulated expression of ribosomal proteins, in which we identified 21 proteins belonging to 40 and 60S ribosomal subunits, suggesting relatively elevated levels of ribosomes under oxidizing conditions.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: The oxidized cells may accumulate 'non-functional' ribosomes whereas the reduced cells were in the process of protein biosynthesis and energy production.
source: Hence we speculate that the oxidized cells may accumulate 'non-functional' ribosomes whereas the reduced cells were in the process of protein biosynthesis and energy production.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the ribosomal protein data.

claim: Elevated levels of cytosolic catalase T (Ctt1) and mitochondrial glutaredoxin (Grx2) were detected in the reduced subpopulation.
source: Moreover, elevated levels of cytosolic catalase T (Ctt1) and mitochondrial glutaredoxin (Grx2) were detected in the reduced subpopulation, likely preserving the reduced state of these cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: Elevated levels of Ctt1 and Grx2 likely preserve the reduced state of these cells.
source: Moreover, elevated levels of cytosolic catalase T (Ctt1) and mitochondrial glutaredoxin (Grx2) were detected in the reduced subpopulation, likely preserving the reduced state of these cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the proteomic findings.

claim: The reduced cells showed increased expression levels of proteins associated with stress granules and stress response, such as Hsp30, Ssb1, Sse2, Hsp78, Dhh1, Hrp1, Prt1, and Xrn1.
source: Intriguingly, the reduced cells showed increased expression levels of proteins associated with stress granules and stress response, such as stress-induced heat shock proteins: Hsp30, Hsp70-type chaperone Ssb1, its ATP exchange factor, Sse2, disaggregase Hsp78, as well as the RNA metabolism proteins: DEAD-box helicase Dhh1, pre-mRNA cleavage protein Hrp1, translational factor Prt1, exonuclease Xrn1 and others (Figure 7—figure supplement 1, Supplementary files 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: These proteins may serve as a first line of defense against oxidation, such that their expression prevents further cellular oxidation.
source: One intriguing possibility is that these proteins serve as a first line of defense against oxidation, such that their expression prevents further cellular oxidation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the proteomic findings.

claim: ∆dhh1 and ∆hsp30 were significantly more oxidized than the wild type over 72 hr.
source: Notably, we found that ∆dhh1 and ∆hsp30 were significantly more oxidized than the wild type over 72 hr (Figure 7A, p-values of the t-test are in Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Hsp30 and Dhh1 were found to be upregulated in the reduced subpopulation, suggesting that they may play a role in redox regulation pathway mediation.
source: Both proteins were found to be upregulated in the reduced subpopulation, suggesting that they may play a role in redox regulation pathway mediation.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the proteomic and deletion strain data.

claim: The Tsa2 knockout had no significant effect on cellular oxidation.
source: Consistent with previously published studies, the Tsa2 knockout had no significant effect on cellular oxidation (Park et al., 2000) (Figure 7A, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis with citation to previous work.

claim: Deletion of the nicotinamidase Pnc1 led to a more reduced environment than in wild type cells, specifically after 48 hr of growth.
source: However, deletion of the nicotinamidase Pnc1, which was found to be upregulated in the oxidized cells, led to a more reduced environment than in wild type cells, specifically after 48 hr of growth (Figure 7A, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Pnc1 may be a potential effector of redox homeostasis.
source: This corresponds with our proteomic analysis and also suggests that Pnc1 may be a potential effector of redox homeostasis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the deletion strain data.

claim: ∆dhh1 was under considerable stress from the onset, with a weaker fluorescent expression and a significantly higher rate of apoptosis as compared to the other strains.
source: Here, we found ∆dhh1 to be under considerable stress from the onset, with a weaker fluorescent expression and a significantly higher rate of apoptosis as compared to the other strains (Mazzoni et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a finding from the confocal microscopy analysis with citation.

claim: Growth rate and replication were stunted in ∆dhh1 in comparison with the other strains.
source: Growth rate and replication were similarly stunted in comparison with the other strains (Duan et al., 2013; Marek and Korona, 2013), in addition to differences in the general appearance of the cells (which were larger and more oval) (Tseng-Rogenski et al., 2003) (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from the microscopy analysis with citations.

claim: A distinct increase in vacuole size was observed in the ∆dhh1 strain.
source: Furthermore, we observed a distinct increase in vacuole size in the ∆dhh1 strain, suggesting Dhh1's role in regulating vacuolar traffic (Chan and Marshall, 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from the microscopy analysis with citation.

claim: Neither ∆pnc1 nor ∆hsp30 display any change in replication or growth.
source: In comparison, neither ∆pnc1 nor ∆hsp30 display any change in replication or growth (Figure 6—figure supplement 3), indeed surpassing the wild type in number of cells after 6 hr growth (Videos 1–4).
evidence: This is a finding from the microscopy analysis.

claim: ∆pnc1 cells on average present as slightly smaller than the wild type, while ∆hsp30 are on average slightly larger than the wild type.
source: Despite no seemingly beneficial impact on their growth rate, both ∆pnc1 and ∆hsp30 display some phenotypic change in regards to size and texture. ∆pnc1 cells on average present as slightly smaller than the wild type, while ∆hsp30 are on average slightly larger than the wild type, yet reproduce at a similar rate.
evidence: This is a finding from the microscopy analysis.

claim: Both ∆pnc1 and ∆hsp30 display small, granule-like clusters within the cell, which may be identified as yeast lipid droplets.
source: Both ∆pnc1 and ∆hsp30, meanwhile, display small, granule-like clusters within the cell, which may be identified as yeast lipid droplets (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from the microscopy analysis with citation.

claim: Deletion of the redox-related proteins affects more than just the average redox status.
source: Together, these results suggest that deletion of the redox-related proteins affects more than just the average redox status, and is worth further investigation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the deletion strain phenotypic data.

claim: ∆tsa2 follows a wild type-like gradual shift towards more highly oxidized ratios.
source: As expected, we observed a gradual shift from the lower (reduced) ratios to more oxidized ratios in the wild type-like ∆tsa2 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from the distribution analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: ∆dhh1 displayed a strong shift towards higher, more oxidized 405/488 nm ratios from early growth (24 hr), with a clear collapse at 72 hr alongside a significant decrease in living cells.
source: Interestingly, ∆dhh1 displayed a strong shift towards higher, more oxidized 405/488 nm ratios from early growth (24 hr), with a clear collapse at 72 hr alongside a significant decrease in living cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a finding from the distribution analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: ∆pnc1 remained largely the same over time, with little change in the dominant fraction of the reduced subpopulation.
source: Conversely, ∆pnc1 remained largely the same over time, with little change in the dominant fraction of the reduced subpopulation (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a finding from the distribution analysis shown in Figure 7E.

claim: ∆hsp30 displayed a unique bimodal distribution that changed little over time.
source: Finally, ∆hsp30 displayed a unique bimodal distribution that changed little over time, explaining its relatively unchanged, moderately high OxD values (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a finding from the distribution analysis shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Hsp30 deletion resulted in the unique bi-modular distribution of the 405/488 nm ratios in the mitochondria but not in the peroxisome.
source: Interestingly, Hsp30 deletion resulted in the unique bi-modular distribution of the 405/488 nm ratios in the mitochondria but not in the peroxisome (Figure 7—figure supplement 3C vs Figure 7—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from the organelle-specific sensor analysis.

claim: Hsp30 may affect the redox synchronization in the mitochondria and cytosol.
source: It is tempting to speculate that Hsp30 affects the redox synchronization in the mitochondria and cytosol.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the organelle-specific data.

claim: Mitochondrial and peroxisomal oxidation was characterized for ∆pnc1 and ∆tsa2 mutants, revealing no significant changes in distribution of the 405/488 nm ratios.
source: Moreover, mitochondrial and peroxisomal oxidation was characterized for ∆pnc1 and ∆tsa2 mutants, revealing no significant changes in distribution of the 405/488 nm ratios (Figure 7—figure supplement 3 vs Figure 7—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the organelle-specific sensor analysis.

claim: In the peroxisome, Dhh1 deletion shifted the oxidation toward higher, more oxidized 405/488 nm ratios.
source: In the peroxisome, however, Dhh1 deletion shifted the oxidation toward higher, more oxidized 405/488 nm ratios (Figure 7—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the peroxisomal sensor analysis.

claim: The identified proteins may contribute to glutathione-dependent redox homeostasis through distinct modes of altering cellular redox state.
source: Together, these results point towards the potential different roles some of the identified proteins in our screen may contribute to glutathione-dependent redox homeostasis, suggesting distinct modes of altering cellular redox state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the deletion strain data.

claim: 4949 genes were identified in the reduced sample and 5027 genes in the oxidized samples.
source: We identified 4949 genes in the reduced sample and 5027 genes in the oxidized samples (Supplementary file 6, 7).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Global changes in the transcriptome were redox- rather than age-dependent.
source: As expected from the proteomic analysis, global changes in the transcriptome were redox- rather than age-dependent (Figure 8A,B, and Figure 7—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: The reduced cells had upregulated carbon metabolism and TCA cycle activity according to annotation analysis of differentially expressed transcripts.
source: Annotation analysis of the differentially expressed transcripts (defined by an at least two-fold change with FDR < 0.05) (Supplementary files 8–11) showed relatively similar functional distributions across transcripts from samples of the same age, which correlates well with the annotation of the abundant proteins in these samples. Specifically, the reduced cells had upregulated carbon metabolism and TCA cycle activity.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic annotation analysis.

claim: The transcriptomic analysis showed that expression of genes involved in lipid biosynthesis and peroxisomal function were upregulated in reduced cells.
source: Interestingly, the transcriptomic analysis showed that expression of genes involved in lipid biosynthesis and peroxisomal function were upregulated.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: The lipid biosynthesis and peroxisomal function upregulation was missing from the proteomic analysis, most probably due to low total abundance of peroxisomal proteins (~1%).
source: This function was missing from the proteomic analysis, most probably due to low total abundance of peroxisomal proteins (~1%).
evidence: This is an interpretation explaining the discrepancy between proteomic and transcriptomic data.

claim: While there is a global correlation in the trend between transcriptomic and proteomic analysis, there are multiple examples of uncoupling in significantly differentially regulated protein and mRNA expression.
source: In examining the general correlation between the transcriptomic and proteomic analysis at 48 and 72 hr (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1), we find that while there is a global correlation in the trend (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1), there are multiple examples of uncoupling in significantly differentially regulated protein and mRNA expression (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, dark red and purple bold circles).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing the transcriptomic and proteomic data.

claim: Expression of transcripts involved in regulatory roles and aging have been found to partially decouple from protein expression.
source: While other studies have shown that protein expression typically corresponds with mRNA expression, expression of transcripts involved in regulatory roles (Marguerat et al., 2012) and aging (Janssens et al., 2015; Wei et al., 2015) have been found to partially decouple.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Although proteins of Hsp30 and Yro2 were upregulated in the reduced cells, their transcripts were shown to be upregulated in the oxidized cells.
source: One of the intriguing examples is Hsp30 and its homologue, Yro2. Although proteins of these genes were upregulated in the reduced cells, their transcripts were shown to be upregulated in the oxidized cells.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing the transcriptomic and proteomic data.

claim: Cellular oxidation might have a differential impact on the half-life time of Hsp30 mRNA and protein molecules, enhancing Hsp30 protein degradation upon elevated oxidation, maintaining high levels of its transcripts over protein molecules.
source: We may speculate that cellular oxidation might have a differential impact on the half-life time of Hsp30 mRNA and protein molecules, that is, enhancing Hsp30 protein degradation upon elevated oxidation, maintaining high levels of its transcripts over protein molecules.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the Hsp30 data.

claim: While Hsp30 had a significant impact on the redox status of cells, its orthologue Yro2 did not.
source: While Hsp30 had a significant impact on the redox status of cells, as we have already shown, its orthologue Yro2 did not.
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis.

claim: Chaperones Hsp78 and Sse2, which showed no significant redox-dependent change in their transcript levels, had no influence on the cellular oxidation.
source: In addition, chaperones Hsp78 and Sse2, which showed no significant redox-dependent change in their transcript levels, had no influence on the cellular oxidation.
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis.

claim: A subset of cells maintained their newly reduced state for over 12 hr, indicating a strong mechanism for maintaining a reduced environment within the cell.
source: Interestingly, a subset of these cells maintained their newly reduced state for over 12 hr (the length of the measurement), indicating a strong mechanism for maintaining a reduced environment within the cell (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9C.

claim: The majority of the reduced cells were able to 'self-correct' their oxidative status for relatively prolonged periods or for a shorter time before undergoing oxidation.
source: The majority of the reduced cells were able to 'self-correct' their oxidative status for relatively prolonged periods (Figure 9D) or for a shorter time (Figure 9E) before undergoing oxidation.
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9D,E.

claim: This self-correction process existed only below a clear oxidation threshold, at an OxD* of approximately 0.7.
source: Surprisingly, this self-correction process existed only below a clear oxidation threshold, at an OxD* of approximately 0.7 (Figure 9C–E).
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9C-E.

claim: Cells were able to reach OxD*s as high as 0.65 before returning to more reduced values as low as 0.4.
source: Cells were able to reach OxD*s as high as 0.65 before returning to more reduced values as low as 0.4, at which state they could remain for several hours before crossing the threshold and undergoing rapid oxidation.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the time-lapse imaging.

claim: Once cells crossed the oxidation threshold, they were unable to correct their oxidative status and maintained high OxD* values until their eventual cell death.
source: However, we observed that once cells crossed the oxidation threshold, they were unable to correct their oxidative status and maintained high OxD* values until their eventual cell death (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9A.

claim: A cluster of newly born daughter cells began life at different time points from a wide range of OxD*s, undergoing a simple oxidation process over time with little deviation or correction.
source: Meanwhile, a cluster of newly born daughter cells began life at different time points from a wide range of OxD*s, undergoing a simple oxidation process over time with little deviation or correction (Figure 9F).
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9F.

claim: In cases of old mother cells with upwards of 10 divisions, the mother cell's age has an impact on its daughters, leading to reduced lifespans in the new daughter cells.
source: Previous research has indicated that in cases of old mother cells with upwards of 10 divisions, the mother cell's age has an impact on its daughters (Kennedy et al., 1994), leading to reduced lifespans in the new daughter cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Mother and daughter cells had identical OxD* values throughout division and immediately following separation, regardless of the length of division or the mother's initial OxD*.
source: Remarkably, we observed that mother and daughter cells had identical OxD* values throughout division and immediately following separation, regardless of the length of division or the mother's initial OxD* (Figure 10A–C), thus demonstrating that daughter cells inherited even a relatively highly oxidized environment during budding.
evidence: This is a finding from the budding cell imaging shown in Figure 10A-C.

claim: Daughter cells inherited even a relatively highly oxidized environment during budding.
source: Remarkably, we observed that mother and daughter cells had identical OxD* values throughout division and immediately following separation, regardless of the length of division or the mother's initial OxD* (Figure 10A–C), thus demonstrating that daughter cells inherited even a relatively highly oxidized environment during budding.
evidence: This is a finding from the budding cell imaging shown in Figure 10A-C.

claim: Some daughter cells were able to self-correct their inherited OxD* levels once the budding process was completed and were able to reach a more reduced state within less than an hour.
source: Moreover, some daughter cells were able to self-correct their inherited OxD* levels once the budding process was completed and were able to reach a more reduced state within less than an hour, even as the mothers crossed the oxidation threshold or maintained their original OxD* (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is a finding from the budding cell imaging shown in Figure 10C.

claim: The influence a mother cell has on her daughters may play a more central role in the oxidative stress of the daughter cell in early life.
source: These findings could suggest that the influence a mother cell has on her daughters may play a more central role in the oxidative stress of the daughter cell in early life.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the budding cell imaging data.

claim: Phenotypic heterogeneity within genetically homogenous cell populations is considered one of the strategies for dealing with fluctuating environments and stress conditions.
source: Phenotypic heterogeneity within genetically homogenous cell populations is considered one of the strategies for dealing with fluctuating environments and stress conditions (Elowitz et al., 2002; Maamar et al., 2007; Avery, 2006; Bishop et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Studies in bacteria and yeast have revealed that cell-to-cell variation is encoded in the stochasticity of gene and protein expression in a normal or changing environment.
source: Studies in bacteria and yeast have revealed that cell-to-cell variation is encoded in the stochasticity of gene and protein expression in a normal or changing environment.
evidence: This is a general statement based on established knowledge.

claim: Diverse mechanisms have been suggested for cell-to-cell variation, ranging from promoter activation and deactivation, the rate of mRNA and protein production, protein and gene modifications, and even metabolic exchange between cells.
source: Diverse mechanisms have been suggested, ranging from promoter activation and deactivation, the rate of mRNA and protein production, protein and gene modifications, and even metabolic exchange between cells (Campbell et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The typical readout of cell-to-cell variation processes is diversity in protein expression leading to differential growth under standard or stress conditions.
source: The typical readout of these processes is diversity in protein expression leading to differential growth under standard or stress conditions.
evidence: This is a general statement based on established knowledge.

claim: The study identified a new type of glutathione-dependent heterogeneity, originating in the redox status of cells, by focusing on cytoplasmic oxidation alongside chronological and replicative aging.
source: Here, we identified a new type of glutathione-dependent heterogeneity, originating in the redox status of cells, by focusing on cytoplasmic oxidation alongside chronological and replicative aging.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's main contribution.

claim: The redox status (up to 72 hr growth in standard medium) is a contributing factor in cellular growth and division properties.
source: Using a self-established, non-laborious methodology to quantify and isolate cells with different oxidation levels, we suggest that the redox status (up to 72 hr growth in standard medium) is a contributing factor in cellular growth and division properties.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: The transition from reduced to oxidized status is a threshold-based phenomenon that leads to the emergence of at least two distinct cell subpopulations with different growth potential and biochemical profiles.
source: Nevertheless, on the basis of our monitoring the time-line of cellular oxidation in aging cells in culture, it is tempting to speculate that the transition from reduced to oxidized status is a threshold-based phenomenon that leads to the emergence of at least two distinct cell subpopulations with different growth potential and biochemical profiles.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: The detection of the redox status of aging yeast cells was based on the cytosolic redox-dependent fluorescent probe, Grx1-roGFP2, which depends on GSH/GSSG levels.
source: Our detection of the redox status of aging yeast cells was based on the cytosolic redox-dependent fluorescent probe, Grx1-roGFP2, which depends on GSH/GSSG levels.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The roGFP probes are well-established indicators of in-vivo redox potentials in bacteria, C. elegans, yeast, plants, and mammals.
source: The roGFP probes are well-established indicators of in-vivo redox potentials in bacteria (van der Heijden and Finlay, 2015), C. elegans (Braeckman et al., 2016), yeast (Morgan et al., 2011), plants (Meyer et al., 2007), and mammals (Dooley et al., 2004), monitoring differences in oxidative stress under a range of diverse conditions.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The utilization of FACS combines the advantages of fluorescence measurement at the level of the individual cell with a high throughput ability to isolate living cells according to their redox-related properties.
source: Our utilization of FACS combines the advantages of fluorescence measurement at the level of the individual cell with a high throughput ability to isolate living cells according to their redox-related properties.
evidence: This describes the advantages of the methodology developed in the study.

claim: Due to the robustness of the Grx1-roGFP2 sensor, the parameters used to define the oxidation gates to quantify the redox levels in the cytosol, mitochondria and peroxisome were very similar.
source: Due to the robustness of the Grx1-roGFP2 sensor, the parameters used to define the oxidation gates to quantify the redox levels in the cytosol, mitochondria and peroxisome were very similar.
evidence: This describes a property of the methodology.

claim: The discrimination between reduced and oxidized cells was clear-cut, enabling rapid and convenient measurements of biologically different samples collected at different days and conditions.
source: The discrimination between reduced and oxidized cells was clear-cut, enabling rapid and convenient measurements of biologically different samples collected at different days and conditions.
evidence: This describes a property of the methodology.

claim: These oxidation gates can be applied to any population of yeast cells expressing the roGFP2 variants to define the contribution of a specific gene or condition on cytosolic redox status or in organelles.
source: These oxidation gates can be applied to any population of yeast cells expressing the roGFP2 variants to define the contribution of a specific gene or condition on cytosolic redox status or in organelles.
evidence: This describes the potential applications of the methodology.

claim: Measurements of this sort may be conducted on a larger scale using knockout-library arrays, ultimately scanning a wide range of mutations and their redox impact across several days.
source: Measurements of this sort may thus be conducted on a larger scale using knockout-library arrays, ultimately scanning a wide range of mutations and their redox impact across several days.
evidence: This describes potential future applications of the methodology.

claim: This approach is not restricted to yeast and may be used in any cell type - from bacteria to mammals.
source: More generally, this approach is not restricted to yeast and may be used in any cell type - from bacteria to mammals.
evidence: This describes the potential broad applicability of the methodology.

claim: Hsp30 is a plasma membrane heat shock protein which is induced by different stress conditions, including heat shock, exposure to ethanol, glucose limitation, oxidation and entry into the stationary phase.
source: Hsp30 is a plasma membrane heat shock protein which is induced by different stress conditions, including heat shock, exposure to ethanol, glucose limitation, oxidation and entry into the stationary phase (Piper et al., 1994; Seymour and Piper, 1999; Thakur and Chakrabarti, 2010; Kim et al., 2006)
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: During heat shock, deletion of Hsp30 leads to inhibition of the Pma1H+ -ATPase, preserving cellular ATP levels.
source: During heat shock, deletion of Hsp30 leads to inhibition of the Pma1H+ -ATPase, preserving cellular ATP levels (Panaretou and Piper, 1992).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Deletion of Hsp30 is correlated with a decrease in superoxide dismutase (sod1) expression.
source: Moreover, deletion of Hsp30 is correlated with a decrease in superoxide dismutase (sod1) expression (Thakur and Chakrabarti, 2010), which might correspond with elevated cellular oxidation.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The transcriptomic and proteomic analysis revealed an opposite regulation profile of Hsp30, pointing to an upregulation of gene expression under an oxidizing environment after 48 and 72 hr of growth, alongside downregulation at the protein level at the same time.
source: Interestingly, our transcriptomic and proteomic analysis revealed an opposite regulation profile of Hsp30, pointing to an upregulation of gene expression under an oxidizing environment after 48 and 72 hr of growth, alongside downregulation at the protein level at the same time.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic and proteomic analyses.

claim: Deletion of Hsp30 led to a significant increase in cellular oxidation, suggesting that high Hsp30 protein levels keep the cells reduced.
source: Moreover, deletion of Hsp30 led to a significant increase in cellular oxidation, suggesting that indeed high Hsp30 protein levels keep the cells reduced.
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis.

claim: The proteomics analysis showed that upregulation of Hsp30 in the reduced cells was coupled with its native partners, all of which were upregulated in the reduced cells.
source: The proteomics analysis showed that upregulation of Hsp30 in the reduced cells was coupled with its native partners, all of which were upregulated in the reduced cells (Figure 6C: Dhh1, catalase Ctt1, chaperones Hsp78 and Sse2, Hxt5, and Yro2).
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: An antagonistic abundance in the RNA and protein levels suggests a potential impairment of Hsp30 protein turnover in oxidized cells.
source: An antagonistic abundance in the RNA and protein levels suggests a potential impairment of Hsp30 protein turnover in oxidized cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transcriptomic and proteomic data.

claim: Gene expression of Hsp30 is induced upon oxidation but protein translation is not efficient enough to sustain levels of Hsp30 that would maintain the reducing environment.
source: Most probably, gene expression is induced upon oxidation but protein translation is not efficient enough to sustain levels of Hsp30 that would maintain the reducing environment.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the Hsp30 data.

claim: Enhanced protein turnover (either due to low translation rates or high proteolysis rates) may push the transcriptional machinery to produce high levels of Hsp30 mRNA without reaching critical protein concentration that serves as a 'redox keeper' of yeast cells.
source: Thus, enhanced protein turnover (either due to low translation rates or high proteolysis rates) may push the transcriptional machinery to produce high levels of Hsp30 mRNA without reaching critical protein concentration that serves as a 'redox keeper' of yeast cells.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the Hsp30 data.

claim: Analysis of the cellular oxidation pointed to a unique bi-modular distribution of distinct reduced and oxidized populations of cells that are preserved during chronological aging in ∆hsp30.
source: Furthermore, analysis of the cellular oxidation (405/488 nm fluorescence intensities) pointed to a unique bi-modular distribution of distinct reduced and oxidized populations of cells that are preserved during chronological aging.
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis.

claim: Hsp30 enhances redox heterogeneity.
source: This suggests that Hsp30 enhances redox heterogeneity, and represents a fascinating role for Hsp30 that may be investigated further in the future.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the deletion strain data.

claim: Dhh1 is a highly conserved RNA DEAD-box helicase, whose protein levels are upregulated in the reduced cells and whose deletion leads to elevated oxidation from early stages of cell growth.
source: In addition to Hsp30, we identified another potential 'redox keeper', a highly conserved RNA DEAD-box helicase Dhh1, whose protein levels are upregulated in the reduced cells and whose deletion leads to elevated oxidation from early stages of cell growth.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic and deletion strain analyses.

claim: Dhh1 is a stress granule-associated helicase, involved in mRNA metabolism.
source: Dhh1 is a stress granule-associated helicase, involved in mRNA metabolism (Buchan et al., 2010; Swisher and Parker, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Deletion of the dhh1 gene led to a global cellular collapse, altering growth, morphology, and possibly inducing high rates of apoptosis.
source: In contrast to Hsp30, deletion of the dhh1 gene led to a global cellular collapse, altering growth, morphology, and possibly inducing high rates of apoptosis.
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis.

claim: Changes in cellular oxidation in ∆dhh1 might be a secondary effect accompanying growth arrest.
source: Therefore, changes in cellular oxidation might be a secondary effect accompanying growth arrest.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ∆dhh1 phenotype.

claim: Other stress granule-associated proteins were upregulated in the reduced cells, including Hrp1, Tif3, Xrn1, and Prt.
source: Interestingly, other stress granule-associated proteins were upregulated in the reduced cells, including mRNA cleavage factor Hrp1, the translation initiation factor eIF-4B, Tif3, 5'−3' exonuclease, Xrn1, and the eIF3b subunit of the eIF3 translation initiation factor, Prt.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: Downregulation of stress granule-associated proteins may lead to a collapse in redox status and migration of these proteins to p-bodies for mRNA decay and transcription inhibition.
source: This might suggest that downregulation of these proteins leads to a collapse in redox status and migration of these proteins to p-bodies for mRNA decay and transcription inhibition.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the proteomic data.

claim: Transcripts of stress granule-associated proteins (except Hrp1) did not show significant change, suggesting that protein turnover or translation rate might play a significant role in the redox homeostasis, rather than gene expression.
source: Interestingly, transcripts of all these proteins, except Hrp1, did not show significant change, suggesting that protein turnover or translation rate might play a significant role in the redox homeostasis, rather than gene expression.
evidence: This is an interpretation comparing the proteomic and transcriptomic data.

claim: Pnc1 was found to be upregulated in the oxidized cells.
source: In contrast to the positive effect of Dhh1 and Hsp30, the nicotinamidase Pnc1 was found to be upregulated in the oxidized cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the proteomic analysis.

claim: The Pnc1 null mutant had lower OxD levels than the wild type, suggesting that Pnc1 deficiency in cells with normal redox status might lead to reducing stress.
source: The null mutant had lower OxD levels than the wild type, suggesting that Pnc1 deficiency in cells with normal redox status might lead to reducing stress, while in oxidized cells its upregulation might have a different effect.
evidence: This is a finding from the deletion strain analysis with interpretation.

claim: Deletion of Pnc1 increases nicotinamide levels, which inhibit the histone deacetylase Sir2 and lead to apoptosis or a decrease in life span.
source: Previous studies have shown that deletion of Pnc1 increases nicotinamide levels, which inhibit the histone deacetylase Sir2 and lead to apoptosis or a decrease in life span (Anderson et al., 2003; Belenky et al., 2007; Gallo et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pnc1 might serve as a link between increased reduced stress, nicotinase accumulation, and a decrease in cell viability.
source: Thus, we propose that Pnc1 might serve as a link between increased reduced stress, nicotinase accumulation, and a decrease in cell viability.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation connecting the Pnc1 data to previous findings.

claim: There were cells with increased OxD values but no division scars in a genetically identical population.
source: Until now it was believed that most oxidative stress comes from age-dependent damage or genetic alterations. However, an intriguing observation of our study is that there were cells with increased OxD values but no division scars in a genetically identical population.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: When examining the distribution of oxidation levels across 12 hr, there was a clear decrease in the number of reduced cells over time, with the peak shifting towards oxidized, Grx1-roGFP2-negative and damaged cells.
source: When examining the distribution of oxidation levels across 12 hr, as expected, we found a clear decrease in the number of reduced cells over time, with the peak shifting towards oxidized, Grx1-roGFP2-negative and damaged cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse imaging.

claim: The redox status of cells fluctuated with time, suggesting the activity of a self-repair mechanism until a specific threshold is reached, approximately 70% of maximal oxidation.
source: Notably, the redox status of cells fluctuated with time, suggesting the activity of a self-repair mechanism until a specific threshold is reached, approximately 70% of maximal oxidation; above this threshold, cells remain permanently oxidized.
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse imaging with interpretation.

claim: The oxidation level of daughter cells was identical to that of their mother cells, lasting for several hours 'after birth'.
source: Analysis of the daughter cells revealed that their oxidation level was identical to that of their mother cells, lasting for several hours 'after birth'.
evidence: This is a finding from the budding cell imaging.

claim: Since the oxidized state received by the daughter cells from the mother is maintained for several hours, and thus exceeds their duplication time, it is suspected to be a regulated mechanism and not simple diffusion of the Grx1-roGFP2 sensor with predefined oxidation.
source: Since the oxidized state received by the daughter cells from the mother is maintained for several hours, and thus exceeds their duplication time, we suspect it is a regulated mechanism and not simple diffusion of the Grx1-roGFP2 sensor with predefined oxidation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the budding cell imaging data.
